text:
Dorr Township posts property assessment notices online, appeal period begins
H. F. Dowd
Assessment notices for property owners in Dorr Township have been posted online, according to a July 22 announcement from McHenry County officials. Property owners can access their assessments through the McHenry County Property Tax Inquiry Portal. For those using computers and tablets, the “Property Assessments Notice” link is available on the right-hand side of their property tax information page. On smartphones, users can find the Assessments tab by clicking the three-line menu icon in the upper right-hand corner.
Officials said that these assessment notices are not property tax bills. The 2026 assessments will be used to determine taxable values for next year’s property taxes. Notices also include information about existing exemptions and list other available exemptions.
Dorr Township residents have a 30-day window from July 22 to file an appeal with the McHenry County Board of Review, ending at midnight on Friday, Aug. 21. Appeals can be filed by visiting the McHenry County Assessments webpage.
This year and going forward, properties in McHenry County that are only adjusted by their equalization factor will no longer receive mailed copies of their assessments. Physical notices will still be sent for re-evaluations, farmland, and new properties. Officials said this change was made to save taxpayers more than $65,000 annually in postage costs.
The county encourages property owners to sign up for email alerts and text messages when assessment notices are published for their township via the Assessments Office website. Assessment notices have already been posted for Richmond and Chemung townships; Richmond’s appeal deadline is midnight Thursday, Aug. 6, while Chemung’s deadline is Thursday, Aug. 13.
The average student-to-teacher ratio in McHenry County was 14-to-1 during the 2022-23 school year with a total enrollment of 45,580 students across county schools; Huntley High School had both the highest enrollment of white students (2,133) and multiracial students (135), Harvard High School had the highest Hispanic student enrollment (574), Harry D. Jacobs High School recorded the highest Black student enrollment (87), and teacher absenteeism was recorded at 34.2%, slightly below Illinois’ state average, according to the Illinois State Board of Education.
